subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — shared vs dedicated isolation (noisy neighbor & SLOs)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@saasco.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@saasco.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up — shared vs dedicated isolation

Elena — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps below so we’re all aligned.

Call recap:
- Primary workload: synchronous chat completions (context ~2-4k tokens).
- Peak throughput: ~150 req/s typical, up to ~400 req/s during marketing events.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end <= 300ms for the user request path.
- Main concerns: noisy-neighbor effects on the hosted/shared API during bursts, isolation boundaries between tenants, and predictable SLOs for latency and throughput.
- Compliance: SOC 2 and US data residency are important for procurement.

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to go live but shared pools can see transient latency variance during noisy bursts.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (customer-only) with configurable throughput and stronger isolation — recommended when you need predictable p95 latency under bursty traffic.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation and customer-managed control plane for regulated workloads.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-capacity-one-pager.pdf attached (high-level SKU and isolation guarantees).

Next steps:
1) I’ll send a short one-pager on Dedicated + a checklist for Private VPC. (attached)
2) Can you confirm the 300ms p95 requirement is for the whole user-to-response path or just server-side token latency?
3) Would you be open to a 30-min technical deep dive with our infra lead (Vivek) and solutions engineer (Marissa) to walk SLOs and network setup? Proposed slots below.

Proposed times (PST): Thu 11/05 10:00am, Thu 11/05 2:00pm, Fri 11/06 9:00am — let me know what works.

Thanks — looking forward to narrowing down the right deployment mode.

--
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@saasco.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@saasco.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — shared vs dedicated isolation

Thanks, Priyom — good summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) The 300ms p95 is our target for the full user-visible response (client -> service -> client). We understand there are network components on our end; we’re primarily concerned about the server-side variance that could push us over that threshold during spikes.

2) On noisy neighbor: can you define the kinds of incidents you’ve observed on shared pools? Are these primarily memory/kv cache eviction effects, GPU saturation from other tenants, or network oversubscription?

3) For Dedicated: do you provide explicit latency SLOs (e.g., committed p95 token latency ranges) and how are those measured? Is there a way to guarantee isolation for bursty spikes (i.e., reserved throughput or capacity buffers)?

4) Compliance: can you share SOC 2 documentation and a high-level description of audit logs (retention, access)? Procurement will want to see that early.

Last — do you have any ballpark pricing tiers for Dedicated vs Private VPC so we can flag budgets to procurement?

Happy to take the technical deep dive — Thu 11/05 2:00pm PST works for me (Elena) and I’ll loop Tom for procurement/terms.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform Engineering | SaaSCo
elena.rossi@saasco.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@saasco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@saasco.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — shared vs dedicated isolation

Elena — great questions, answered inline below. I’ve also attached the Dedicated one-pager and a Private VPC checklist.

1) Noisy-neighbor root causes we see on shared pools:
   - GPU saturation from other tenants on the same host (rare but possible during large model requests).
   - KV cache churn causing increased memory pressure and higher token generation latency for hot prefixes.
   - Burst networking contention in specific region-level shared fabric (we mitigate via multi-az routing).

2) Dedicated guarantees and measurements:
   - Dedicated = reserved GPU pools isolated to your tenancy; noisy-neighbor from other customers is effectively eliminated.
   - We expose token-level latency metrics and per-connection throughput; SLOs are measured at the model route level (p50/p95/p99) from our edge to the serving runtime.
   - For bursty spikes we offer configurable reserved throughput and optional burst buffers — you can commit to an X req/s baseline and allow Y burst for a window.

3) Typical p95 token latency numbers (example, depends on model/seq length):
   - Small open LLM (quantized, short context): p95 token latency ~20-50ms
   - Medium LLM (2-4k context): p95 token latency ~50-120ms
   - Larger context runs or heavy generation: higher — we’ll run numbers against your exact prompt/profile.

4) Compliance/SOC 2: happy to share our SOC 2 Type II report and a summary of audit log retention and access controls. I’ll route that to procurement after we sign an NDA/CA if needed; meanwhile the Private VPC checklist lists our KMS/HSM options.

Pricing/next steps:
- Ballpark: Dedicated starts at a monthly reserved commitment (we’ll send SKU-level pricing in the quote); Private VPC has a platform fee + infra estimate. I’ll follow up with a formal quote once we confirm the expected baseline throughput and desired isolation level.
- Proposed next step: 30-min technical deep dive Thu 11/05 2:00pm PST — Marissa (solutions) and Vivek (infra) will join to walk SLOs and the network diagram. Please let us know who from procurement will join.
- POC option: we can run a limited Dedicated trial (14-30 days) with reserved capacity to validate p95 under your traffic profile.

If you can send a short doc with expected concurrent requests, average tokens per request, and any compliance checklist items, we’ll bring a tailored proposal to the call.

Thanks — attaching: redwood-dedicated-capacity-one-pager.pdf, redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf

--
